summary: COP31 runs into a second overtime day, Russian missiles land in Poland, Hormuz attacks climb, Gaza's peace plan stalls, AI stocks slide, and talks on 'killer robots' inch ahead.

question.text: Iran says a tanker hit a mine while shipping monitors report projectile strikes; Israel and a witness describe the people in a Gaza van differently. When the only witnesses are the sides involved, what kinds of evidence would make you trust one account more than another?

read.title: Russian missiles hit Poland: What happened, and could NATO respond?
read.summary: An explainer on where the missiles fell, what NATO's Article 4 and Article 5 actually require, and why experts think Russia may be testing how far it can push the alliance.

topics.heading: COP31 enters a second day of overtime as new text skips any direct fossil-fuel wording
topics.summary: The UN climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye, was still unfinished on Sunday, more than 40 hours past its deadline.[^2][^3] A revised text refers back to the 2023 pledge to move away from fossil fuels without naming coal, oil or gas, and France called it unacceptable.[^1][^2]

lead.title: COP31 struggles to reach deal with parties at odds over fossil fuels

alsoReported.title: France slams new draft as COP31 could be longest climate summit ever
COP31 climate deal in the balance after fractious talks

article: Yesterday's brief left COP31 in overtime. By Sunday it was still going. The summit's Turkish president, Murat Kurum, released a revised final text early Sunday and gave countries until 03:00 GMT to object, with a session to approve it set for 06:00 GMT.[^1][^4] As of Sunday morning, Reuters reported that a deal was "far from certain".[^3]

The new text does not name coal, oil or gas. Instead it points back to the 2023 Dubai pledge to transition away from fossil fuels.[^1][^2] It keeps a goal of raising electricity's share of final energy use to 35% by 2035, calls for faster carbon capture and storage (trapping CO2 before it reaches the air), and repeats a promise to triple adaptation funding by 2035 without an interim target.[^1][^2] It also accepts that warming will pass 1.5C and asks that any overshoot be small and short.[^2]

Kurum said he believed the text was one "all the parties can agree upon" and that concerns on fossil fuels and adaptation money had been addressed.[^4] France's environment minister, Monique Barbut, disagreed, calling it "even weaker than the previous one" and saying an overnight EU compromise had been rejected.[^2] More than 100 civil society groups warned it could be one of the most disappointing COPs ever.[^4]

Background: every COP decision needs consensus, which lets a single bloc slow things down. DPA notes that formal decisions also need enough countries in the room, and many ministers had already gone home.[^2] Reuters says the main splits are the pace of the clean-energy shift, carbon capture, and money for developing countries.[^3]
My read: a deal is still the most likely outcome, since only one COP has ever ended without one.[^1] But whether a text that does not name fossil fuels counts as progress will depend on who you ask.
topics.differences: COP31 president Murat Kurum says no one got everything they wanted but everyone can find a place in the text.[^3] France calls it unacceptable and weaker than before.[^2] Earlier drafts dropped fossil-fuel wording after objections from Saudi Arabia and other producers.[^4] Critics also say electrification should run on renewables, not gas or coal.[^1]

topics.heading: Russian missiles and a drone land in Poland during a huge overnight attack on Ukraine
topics.summary: Two Russian missiles and a suspected drone came down in southeastern Poland, a NATO member, during a massive Russian strike on Ukraine; no one in Poland was hurt.[^5][^6] Poland's prime minister called it an "intentional provocation", and NATO called it a "grave violation" of Polish airspace.[^5][^7]

lead.title: NATO calls Russian missiles landing in Poland a 'grave violation' of airspace

alsoReported.title: Poland accuses Russia of "intentional provocation" as missiles hit NATO soil, kill at least 8 in Ukraine
Russian strike kills two, wounds 60, in Zelenskyy's hometown

article: Overnight into Friday, Russia launched one of its largest attacks of the war. Ukraine's president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, said it involved more than 400 drones and about 110 missiles, and Ukrainian officials said at least eight civilians were killed.[^6][^7] Russia's Defence Ministry said it hit targets linked to Ukraine's military.[^5] President Vladimir Putin had promised retaliation for a Ukrainian strike on the Kerch Bridge to Crimea.[^6]

During the attack, Poland says two missiles, believed to be Kh-101 cruise missiles, and a jet-powered drone landed on its territory, about 30 to 50 km from the Ukrainian border. No injuries or damage were reported.[^5][^7] The landings came during a two-week European military exercise in Poland that prepares for a possible post-war mission in Ukraine.[^5]

Prime Minister Donald Tusk said it looked like "an intentional provocation", and Poland's defence minister said the timing was hard to see as a coincidence.[^6] NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte called it a "grave violation" and "clearly dangerous".[^5] Moscow had not commented on the landings.[^5]

Background a student needs: NATO's Article 5 says an attack on one member is an attack on all, but using it needs political agreement and is not automatic. Article 4 only means emergency talks; Poland has not invoked it this time.[^7] Separately, a Russian strike on Kryvyi Rih, Zelenskyy's hometown, killed two people and injured 60, according to local officials.[^8]

All this happens while the US pushes peace talks. Zelenskyy said he is less sure than Washington that Putin is ready to compromise, and Moscow still demands that Ukraine leave the whole Donbas region.[^8] Experts quoted by Al Jazeera expect a defensive NATO response, such as more air patrols, rather than escalation.[^7]
topics.differences: Poland's leaders say the landings were deliberate.[^6] NATO calls them dangerous and a result of Russia's war.[^5] One analyst quoted by Al Jazeera describes them as spillover from strikes on Ukraine, while another sees Russia testing NATO's limits.[^7] Russia had not commented.[^5]

topics.heading: More tankers hit near Hormuz as Iran tightens its grip on Gulf shipping
topics.summary: Two tankers were struck near Oman's coast on Saturday, and Iran says a third caught fire after hitting a mine.[^9] Iran says it controls the Strait of Hormuz and that ships must follow its rules, while talks to end the war remain stuck.[^9][^10]

lead.title: Tankers hit in Strait of Hormuz as Iran tightens grip on shipping

alsoReported.title: Iran says it downed US drones over Hormuz as bid to end war remains stalled

article: The Strait of Hormuz is a narrow sea passage between Iran and Oman. Before the war it carried nearly a fifth of the world's crude oil.[^9] The war began in late February when the US and Israel attacked Iran, and the US has since blockaded Iranian ports and escorted tankers through the waterway.[^9]

On Saturday, the UK's maritime monitoring centre, UKMTO, reported two tankers hit by unidentified projectiles near the Omani town of Khasab, with no injuries.[^9] Iran's navy said a tanker caught fire after hitting a mine in a restricted area, claiming the ship ignored warnings and had its tracking switched off; that could not be independently checked.[^9] Iran says ships must use lanes it chooses.[^9]

The pace is rising. Citing Iranian military statements, Al Jazeera's Tehran correspondent counted about 25 incidents involving tankers in the week since last Saturday, roughly three a day.[^9] He said Tehran is escalating on purpose to signal that if Iran cannot export oil, others will not be able to either.[^9] The US has answered with its blockade, tanker escorts, and new sanctions on four Iranians it says collected money from illegal oil sales.[^9][^10]

Diplomacy is not moving much. Iran's foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, listed seven conditions for reopening the strait, including ending the war, lifting sanctions and lifting the blockade, and ruled out sending Iran's enriched uranium abroad.[^10] President Trump said Iran wants a deal, but not one he would accept.[^10] Iran's Revolutionary Guards also said they shot down two US drones; the US had not commented.[^10]

Araghchi called the current "no war, no peace" situation undesirable.[^10] In Washington, some Democrats want Congress to block money for offensive operations against Iran in a spending bill due by December 11.[^10] My read: the stand-off matters far beyond the Gulf, because oil prices feed into fuel and food costs everywhere, including Canada.
topics.differences: Iran says the burning tanker hit a mine after ignoring warnings and switching off its tracking; that could not be independently verified.[^9] The UK monitoring centre describes two ships hit by unidentified projectiles, and it is unclear whether either is the ship Iran describes.[^9]

topics.heading: US-led Board of Peace warns it may hand Gaza to the UN if Israel keeps blocking its plan
topics.summary: A senior adviser to the US-controlled Board of Peace said it could "hand the keys" of Gaza to the UN if Israel keeps blocking steps to disarm Hamas and rebuild.[^11] Meanwhile Israeli strikes killed at least nine people on Friday and Saturday, according to Palestinian sources, including three in a van carrying food.[^12][^13]

lead.title: Board of Peace will give UN 'the keys' to Gaza if Israel won't honor commitments, official warns

alsoReported.title: Israeli strike on vehicle distributing food aid in Gaza kills three
IDF strikes PIJ terrorist's vehicle in Gaza, following claims it was used by aid workers

article: The Board of Peace was set up in January to carry out President Trump's 20-point plan for Gaza, after a ceasefire took effect in October 2025.[^11] On Friday, its senior adviser Josh Gruenbaum told the Israeli outlet Ynet that the board would hand Gaza to the UN if Israel keeps blocking its work.[^11][^12]

Gruenbaum said the board is not asking Israel to withdraw. It wants Israel to approve an International Stabilization Force, a new Palestinian police force and a Palestinian administrative committee.[^11] Without them, he said, there is no one to receive Hamas's weapons. He blamed "political elements" in the government and said not enough aid is entering before winter, while adding that Hamas could still cheat on disarmament.[^11]

Israel held an election on October 27 with no clear winner, and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu leads a caretaker government while coalition talks go on.[^11] Israeli officials told Ynet they prefer the current situation, with Hamas weakened and Israel controlling over half of Gaza.[^11] A board report this week warned the ceasefire could collapse.[^12]

Violence continues. Palestinian sources reported at least nine people killed on Friday and Saturday.[^12] Gaza's Health Ministry says 1,671 people have been killed since the ceasefire began.[^13] Winter rain is worsening conditions for a mostly displaced population.[^12][^13]
My read: the warning is a pressure tactic aimed at Israel's next government. What happens next likely depends on whether a coalition forms and whether Washington follows through.
topics.differences: A witness told Reuters the van hit on Saturday was handing out food to children, and papers inside carried World Central Kitchen's logo; the charity said the vehicle was not theirs.[^13][^14] The Israeli military says the three killed were Palestinian Islamic Jihad members moving supplies for armed groups.[^14]

topics.heading: AI stock sell-off pushes the S&P 500 into a correction and erases the Nasdaq's 2026 gains
topics.summary: US stocks fell sharply on Friday as investors dumped AI-linked shares: the S&P 500 dropped 3.7% and the Nasdaq 5.3%.[^15][^16] Nvidia fell about 13% after Reuters reported that US regulators are looking at its accounting.[^17]

lead.title: Wall Street suffers historic losses as Dow, S&P 500 plunge into correction territory

alsoReported.title: Nvidia's accounting is a focus of US SEC investigation, sources say
How major US stock indexes fared Friday 11/20/2026

article: Friday was a rough day on Wall Street. The S&P 500, a broad index of big US companies, fell 3.7%, the Dow 1.9% and the tech-heavy Nasdaq 5.3%.[^16] The S&P 500 is now in a "correction", meaning it has dropped more than 10% from its record high on October 6.[^16] Over the week, the Nasdaq lost 10%, its worst week since March 2020.[^15][^16]

The selling centred on artificial intelligence stocks. Reuters reported, citing two unnamed people, that the US Securities and Exchange Commission is examining Nvidia's accounting; the SEC declined to comment and Nvidia did not respond at first.[^17] Reuters stressed that an investigation is not proof of wrongdoing.[^17] Nvidia fell about 13% that day and is down about 46% from its October peak.[^17][^18]

Other news added to the worry. Broadcom fell 12% after a report that Google cut its plans for Broadcom's AI chips.[^18] Nvidia is also adjusting to life after Jensen Huang's exit as CEO.[^18] Anthropic, the AI company that set a record for the largest share sale ever on Thursday, fell about 8.5% in its second day of trading.[^15][^19]

Why it matters: the worry spread beyond tech. Fox Business reports that gold rose as investors looked for safer places for their money, and a common measure of market fear hit its highest level since April 2025.[^15] Investors had already been questioning heavy AI spending, losses and debt used to build data centres.[^19]

My read: one bad week does not prove the AI boom is a bubble, and markets often recover from corrections. But it shows how much confidence in AI's payoff is now built into prices, and how quickly that confidence can wobble.

topics.heading: UN weapons talks agree to work on 'killer robot' rules by 2028, but not a binding treaty
topics.summary: Countries meeting in Geneva agreed to spend two years working out possible rules on weapons that can choose and attack targets without a human deciding.[^20][^21] Nearly 100 states wanted binding rules, but the US, Russia and Israel opposed that, and campaigners called the result watered down.[^20]

lead.title: Nations agree to 'elaborate' on rules for AI-run 'killer robots' by 2028

alsoReported.title: UN talks fail to ban AI 'Killer Robots' as 128 States delay rules to 2028

article: Lethal autonomous weapons, often called "killer robots", are systems that can kill without a human making the final decision to fire. Campaigners say some, including AI systems that pick targets, are already used in combat.[^20]

At a UN meeting in Geneva under the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons, 128 countries agreed to "elaborate" a possible agreement on these weapons over the next two years, by 2028.[^20][^21] The word "negotiate" was avoided because some countries rejected it.[^20] Talks ran past 4 a.m. after Russian procedural objections cancelled several sessions earlier in the week.[^21]

The convention works by consensus, so one country can block a proposal.[^21] Nearly 100 nations pushed for legally binding rules, but major weapons makers, including the US, Russia and Israel, opposed that.[^20] It is unclear whether whatever comes out in 2028 will be enforceable.[^21]

The Swiss diplomat who chaired the meeting, Julien Thoeni, called it a significant step after more than ten years of talks and said it shows multilateral diplomacy can still deliver.[^20] Campaign group Stop Killer Robots called the mandate "watered down", and Human Rights Watch said it falls short of what is needed while the technology moves fast.[^20][^21]

Why it matters: armies are adding AI to weapons quickly, while the rules are still being argued over. My read: a two-year plan keeps the issue alive, but what counts is whether the biggest military powers sign up to anything binding.
topics.differences: The chair calls the deal a concrete result after a decade of talks.[^20] Campaigners and Human Rights Watch say it delays binding rules.[^20][^21] The US, Russia and Israel opposed a push for legally binding commitments.[^20]
